correctness.rationale: Strict convexity yields the unique implicit p-mean and translation/cross-coordinate monotonicity, giving global bound n^(1/p). For n=2 symmetry gives a linear arithmetic mean of norm one; at p=2 orthogonal projection has norm one. For 1<p<2, an explicit centered residual configuration with one zero residual produces m(x+epsilon e1)/epsilon→1 because the remaining scalar residual equation is C1 and epsilon−m=O(epsilon^(1/(p−1)))=o(epsilon). For p>2, implicit differentiation gives nonnegative weights summing to one, and the residual stationarity forces every weight at most one-half; hence the conjugate norm is at most 2^(−1/p). Integration along segments (splitting once if a segment meets the diagonal) supplies the global upper bound (n/2)^(1/p), attained infinitesimally at residuals (1,−1,0,...). All quantifiers n>=2, p>1, real scalars, boundary p=2, and n=2 exception are accounted for. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.
risks: Only sharpness as a limit of nearby point pairs is asserted; actual finite-pair attainment is not established.
The proof explicitly assumes a real scalar field and finite-dimensional space; complex or nonatomic cases are excluded.

originality.rationale: The defining literature directly addresses finite-dimensional lp best approximation and proves uniform Lipschitz continuity without computing its exact constant. The later complete 2017 paper explicitly singles out the diagonal all-ones line and gives an upper estimate rather than a sharp value, and its exact formula is not a special case of either the general 1997 theorem or the maximum two-dimensional projection bound. New sharp global constants, the subquadratic/superquadratic transition and discontinuity at p=2 are compared by actual statements and implications, not title coincidence.

value.rationale: The exact stability constant of best ℓp approximation onto the canonical constant-vector line is a natural quantity in nonlinear Chebyshev approximation and p-mean aggregation. The checked 1997 and 2017 sources focus on existence and nonsharp estimates; the new result closes that quantitative gap uniformly for every n and p. It reveals a nontrivial dimension-dependent structural bifurcation at p=2, including an unexpected discontinuity of the optimal global operator Lipschitz norm. The sharp high- and low-p configurations also show why general norm-equivalence continuity is insufficient. This is not an arbitrary instance or routine numerical improvement.
risks: A specialized p-mean literature could contain the sharp constants under terminology not exposed by searches; this is an originality risk.
Only fixed-line stability is settled, not arbitrary target subspaces.
